learning_experiences: in pairs read Genesis 1:27,
say why they are a special creation,
sing songs related to their uniqueness,
state their gender as guided by Genesis 1:27,
draw and colour a picture of a boy and a girl,
in turns read Isaiah 43:1,
write their names on flashcards and display them in class,
sing songs related to their names,
watch a clip of a palm of a hand with a name on it,
draw the palm of a hand and write their names,
Sing the song, ‘I’ am fearfully and wonderfully made’,
memorise Isaiah 49:16.
key_inquiry_questions: What makes you a special creation?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: learners identify who they are as they engage in activities such as mentioning their names and singing songs related to their names.
Communication: learners can speak clearly and effectively as they read the Bible verses and memorise the scriptures.
sub_strands.values: Love is portrayed as learners sing songs and perform activities such as singing together.
sub_strands.pcis: Gender issues: learners say their gender as guided by the Bible and in accordance with the Christian faith.
sub_strands.links:
Language Activities: they learn new vocabulary.
Creative Activities: creative skills are enhanced as they sing and draw.

outcomes.text: identity their uniqueness as guided by the word of God
state their gender according to Genesis 1:27
appreciate that God knows them by their names

skills.name: Identify their uniqueness as God's creation and state their gender (Genesis 1:27)
skills.mastery: Says God made each child special and different (no two children are the same, even twins), that God knows each one by name, and states his or her gender as a boy (male) or girl (female) as God created people male and female (Genesis 1:27). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Knowing God made people comes first. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Saying one's own name. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks twins or siblings are exactly the same person.

example.question: Are twins exactly the same?
example.correct_answer: No, each is special and different

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, the same" beside "No, each is special and different" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Compare thumbprints of two children, or two leaves of one tree.
misconceptions.feedback: Even twins are different. God made each one special.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a girl becomes a boy if she wears trousers or has short hair.

example.question: A girl has short hair. Is she still a girl?
example.wrong_answer: No, she is a boy now

misconceptions.cause: Young children judge gender by clothes and hair.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No, she is a boy now" beside "Yes, she is a girl" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say: God made you a boy or a girl; clothes and hair do not change it.
misconceptions.feedback: Short hair does not change a girl into a boy. God made her a girl.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God does not know small children's names.

example.question: Does God know your name?
example.correct_answer: Yes, God knows me by name

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No, I am too small" beside "Yes, God knows me by name" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say Isaiah 43:1 simply: God says, "I have called you by name."
misconceptions.feedback: God knows you by your name.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks children were made by the hospital or bought.

example.question: Who made you?

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The hospital" beside "God" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Sing a song about God making me. Read Genesis 1:27 with pictures.
misconceptions.feedback: God made you.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

learning_experiences: list names of family members on flashcards,
draw and colour family members,
demonstrate how they pray at home,
list the number of times they pray at home as a family,
mention instances they lead prayers at home,
in groups or pairs, list items they share at home,
colour a picture of a family sharing a meal,
sing the song, ’Read your Bible pray every day’,

key_inquiry_questions: How do you relate with members of your family?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication: the skill of speaking clearly and effectively is enhanced as learners lead prayers at home.
Learning to Learn: learners work on their own in assigned tasks such as listing the number of times they lead prayers at home.
sub_strands.values: Unity is enhanced as learners pray with family members.
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion is portrayed as learners share items with family members and pray together.
sub_strands.links:
Mathematical Activities: learners list the number of times they pray.
Language Activities: reading skills are applied as learners read the Bible.

learning_experiences: say how they take care of the Holy Bible,
tell why they should respect the Holy Bible,
role-play handling the Holy Bible with care and respect,

listen to and sing a song about the Bible,

sub_strands.sub_strand: Bible Story: Joseph and his brothers
learning_experiences: watch a video on Joseph’s coat of many colours in Genesis 37:3-4,
draw a coat and colour it,
in turns, picture-read Joseph’s dream in Genesis 37:5-8,in groups, picture-read Genesis 37:9-11,
role-play the story of Joseph,
say why Joseph’s brothers hated him,
in groups, share experiences of how they should treat their brothers and sisters,
list values needed to live well with others,
sing a song about Joseph and his coat of many colours.
key_inquiry_questions: How did Joseph relate with his brothers?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology is enhanced as learners watch a video about Joseph and his brothers.
Imagination and Creativity: the skill of imagining and coming up with original ideas is exhibited as learners draw and colour a coat.
sub_strands.values: Love is nurtured as learners share experiences of how they should treat their brothers and sisters.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Cohesion is nurtured as learners list values needed to live well with others.
sub_strands.links:
Language Activities: learners picture-read Bible texts.
Creative Activities: learners draw, colour and role-play the story of Joseph.

outcomes.text: narrate the story of Joseph and his brothers

skills.name: Narrate the story of Joseph and his brothers (Genesis 37)
skills.mastery: Narrates Genesis 37: Jacob loved Joseph and gave him a richly coloured coat; his brothers were jealous; Joseph dreamt their sheaves bowed to his; the brothers hated him more and sold him to traders going to Egypt, then told their father a wild animal had killed him. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Listening to and retelling a short Bible story. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Family members, brothers and sisters. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Discuss how to treat siblings and name values for peaceful living
skills.mastery: Says how to treat brothers and sisters well (share, help, play together, say sorry, not fight or tease, not be jealous) and names values for peaceful co-existence: love, sharing, forgiveness, respect, kindness. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: kind or unkind to a sibling
a value for living in peace

Saying sorry and thank you. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

example.question: Who got the coat of many colours?

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "All the brothers" beside "Only Joseph" and ask the child to choose.

misconceptions.feedback: Only Joseph got the special coat.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

skills.name: List the importance of obeying parents (Ephesians 6:1-3)

example.question: Why should children obey parents?
example.correct_answer: God says it is right, and it keeps us safe

misconceptions.cause: Fear is the reason children hear.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "So we are not beaten" beside "God says it is right, and it keeps us safe" and ask the child to choose.

misconceptions.feedback: We obey parents because God says it is right and it keeps us safe.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks obeying later is the same as obeying.

example.question: Mother says "come and eat". When should you come?

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "After my game" beside "Straight away" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Play a game: obey at once when called.
misconceptions.feedback: Obeying means doing it straight away.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks only the mother must be obeyed.

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No" beside "Yes, both parents (and guardians)" and ask the child to choose.

misconceptions.feedback: Obey both your father and mother.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a child must obey any adult, even one asking to keep a secret or go somewhere alone.

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, obey adults" beside "No, say no and tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
